scope: T02c receiver-local trace and iPhone cellular 5G/Ponte; no physical input-to-photon claim

limits: All intervals use one receiver clock. There is no cross-peer clock subtraction.
Last primary ingress is not guaranteed complete assembly: RTX is encrypted and arrives separately.
RTP correlation requires unique timestamps and one ingress primary SSRC. Decode stages require the same exact frame ID.
Display enqueue means API submission, not photons or verified scanout. SDK renderer and display observers are parallel callbacks.
Per-view observer IDs isolate bindings. Long gaps can contain missing frames; they do not by themselves locate a stall.

conditions.network: cellular 5G + Surge Ponte; outer path unknown
conditions.fixture: real Chrome window, moving dense SVG diagram, speed 2; SDR content in Main10 PQ capture

limits: Decode and enqueue counters are not physical screen presentation.
20 Mbps is a configured ceiling; this fixture did not sustain 15–20 Mbps.
Three sequential trials on varying cellular conditions do not establish a fixed improvement percentage.
No freeze/loss occurred in the phone runs; loss-recovery speed remains unverified on this phone.
350 seconds is not the planned 30 minute stability acceptance.
The trace-off run is not an isolated CPU/energy overhead measurement.
RTP/bridge intervals use local clocks, not cross-device one-way latency.
